help.title: Strength Regression
help.body:
Description
Strength Regression

Purpose
Strength Regression estimates the reliability of a system by quantifying the probability that a strength response (e.g. a weld's torque capacity) exceeds a stress load, where strength is modelled as a linear function of a controllable input variable. It provides both a point estimate and a statistically conservative lower-bound reliability at a specified confidence level, grounded in the Reiser & Guttman (1988) framework.

Inputs
Input Variable — the controllable process parameter that drives strength (e.g. Upset distance)
Response Variable — the measured output representing both strength and stress observations in the same column (e.g. Torque)
Categorizing Variable — a grouping column that distinguishes strength rows from stress rows (e.g. Location)
Strength Value — the category label within the Categorizing Variable that identifies the strength observations (e.g. "Weld"); all remaining rows are treated as stress
Confidence Level — statistical confidence for the lower-bound reliability calculation (default 0.95)
Optimize Reliability — finds the Target Input value required to achieve a user-specified Target Reliability (e.g. 0.999)
Calculate Reliability — evaluates the reliability achieved at a user-supplied fixed Target Input value

Output Interpretation
The summary reports the mean and standard deviation of both the stress and strength distributions,
the Target Input (either solved or supplied), and the key reliability metrics.
Est. Reliability is the point estimate of the probability that strength exceeds stress.
L.B. Reliability is the statistically conservative lower bound at the chosen confidence level — this is the figure to use for engineering decisions as it accounts for estimation uncertainty in both the regression and the stress distribution.
Safety Factor provides a traditional deterministic margin check.
Accompanying diagnostic plots show the regression fit with overlaid stress and strength distributions,
residual assumption checks for the strength model, and stability/normality checks for the stress observations.
